title: Vice Versa Statement Swap and Symmetry Check
literalboundary: This UKR defines a language-level vice-versa operator. It describes how to swap roles or sides in a statement for analysis. It is not a plan for impersonation, evasion, harassment, surveillance, or any real-world action.

coresummary.plaintranslation: Vice versa means flipping the roles or sides in a relationship and checking what remains true, what changes, and what breaks.
coresummary.onelinetranslation: Swap A and B in the statement, then see what still holds.

definitions.statement: Any declarative sentence that asserts a relationship, role, or comparison between at least two named parts.
definitions.rolepair: The two elements that will be swapped, usually subject/object, agent/patient, or group A / group B.
definitions.viceversaoperation: A structured procedure that takes a statement and a chosen role pair (A,B), swaps their positions, and then re-evaluates meaning and validity.

fields.context: Optional short description of situation or domain.
fields.roles: List of role labels or entities that appear in the statement.

fields.roleA: First role label or entity to be swapped.
fields.roleB: Second role label or entity to be swapped.
fields.roleAmarkers: Pronouns, names, or noun phrases bound to roleA.
fields.roleBmarkers: Pronouns, names, or noun phrases bound to roleB.

fields.text: Resulting statement text after swapping roleA and roleB markers.
fields.notes: Any adjustments needed to keep grammar readable.

fields.logicalsymmetry: Does the claim stay logically equivalent after swap? values: symmetric, asymmetric, unclear.
fields.fairnesstest: Does the swap reveal bias or double standard? values: same_standard, double_standard, context_dependent.
fields.meaningchange: Short description of what changed in meaning, if anything.
fields.evidenceimpact: Does the swap change what evidence would be needed? values: no_change, changes_required, not_applicable.

governingrule: Every statement and its vice-versa form stay inside their own evidence boundaries. A clean swap may reveal symmetry or bias, but it does not by itself prove guilt, innocence, authority, or moral standing.

falseequations.collapse: Imagination of a swapped statement equals real misconduct.
falseequations.correction: Imagining or writing the swapped statement is a thought exercise, not an action.
Even if statements look symmetric, real-world evidence may differ by context and facts.

falseequations.collapse: Vice versa failure means someone is automatically wrong or malicious.
falseequations.correction: Asymmetry can come from legitimate context differences, not just bias.

processflow.compactflow: capture-statement → identify-role-pair → bind-markers → generate-swapped-statement → evaluate-symmetry → record-conclusions

steps.name: Capture statement
steps.question: What exact statement are we analyzing?
steps.rule: Write the full sentence without paraphrasing.

steps.name: Identify role pair
steps.question: Which two roles or entities are we swapping?
steps.rule: Choose A and B so that swapping them is meaningful (e.g., men/women, boss/employee, groupX/groupY).

steps.name: Bind markers
steps.question: What words in the sentence point to roleA and roleB?
steps.rule: List names, nouns, and pronouns that clearly refer to A and to B.

steps.name: Generate swapped statement
steps.question: What do we get if we swap A-markers and B-markers?
steps.rule: Replace each roleA marker with roleB and each roleB marker with roleA, adjusting grammar only as needed.

steps.name: Evaluate symmetry and fairness
questions: Does the swapped statement still make logical sense?
Would we treat the swapped version as acceptable, true, or fair to say?
Does the swap change what evidence we would demand?
rules: If both versions need the same type and strength of evidence, mark fairnesstest = "same_standard".
If one version is accepted without evidence while the other is condemned, consider fairnesstest = "double_standard".
If context (history, power, law) matters, mark fairnesstest = "context_dependent" and describe why.

steps.name: Record conclusion
steps.question: What did the vice-versa test show?
steps.rule: Keep the conclusion descriptive, not punitive. Stay with what the swap reveals about structure, not about personal worth.

D1_deduction.question: What must be true for vice versa to work?
answers: The statement must identify at least two roles or entities.
We must be able to map words in the sentence to those roles.
Swapping A and B produces a new sentence that can be read and evaluated.

A1_abduction.question: What could a vice-versa result explain?
answers: Why a rule feels fair only in one direction.
Which parts of a claim depend on power, history, or context.
Where hidden bias or double standards might live.

R_reduction.question: What does the vice-versa test actually prove?
answers: It proves how the wording behaves under a clean role swap.
It does not by itself prove legal guilt, moral status, or factual truth.
It highlights where we need more context or evidence.

A2_reconstruction.question: After removing over-interpretation, what remains?
answers: A pair of statements (original and swapped) with noted similarities and differences.
A clearer map of where symmetry holds and where context breaks symmetry.

D2_deduction.question: What final distinction must hold?
answers: Vice versa is a lens on structure and fairness, not a final verdict on people.
Symmetry in language is evidence about framing, not about who is right in reality.

example1.originalstatement: It is fine for bosses to read their employees' public posts, but not the other way around.
example1.swappedstatement: It is fine for employees to read their bosses' public posts, but not the other way around.

evaluation.meaningchange: Same structure; power difference may affect risk but not the core logic of reading public posts.

example2.originalstatement: Group X may stereotype Group Y, but Group Y must never stereotype Group X.
example2.swappedstatement: Group Y may stereotype Group X, but Group X must never stereotype Group Y.

evaluation.meaningchange: Swapping shows that the rule is about who is allowed to stereotype whom, not about stereotyping being wrong in itself.

intendeduse: Test fairness and symmetry of rules, policies, or judgments by swapping roles.
Surface hidden double standards without accusing anyone by default.
Clarify which asymmetries come from real-world context and which come from bias.
hardboundaries: Do not treat vice-versa results as automatic proof of guilt or virtue.
Do not use vice versa to bypass evidence requirements in legal, clinical, or safety decisions.
Keep imagination, wording tests, and real-world conduct clearly separated.
